paper.title_en: The Terrell-Penrose effect revisited and extended for black hole spacetime
paper.abstract_en: Half a century ago, Terrell and Penrose independently studied the visual appearance of a moving sphere and found that the visual distortion can be formulated by a conformal transformation on the observer's celestial sphere. In this study, we examine the Terrell-Penrose effect by considering the images of spheres in two contrasting cases: i) a static sphere in the view of a moving observer, and ii) a moving sphere in the view of a static observer. In these two cases, the images are expected to be identical for flat spacetime because of the principle of relativity. However, utilizing ray-tracing simulations, our results find that the images are distinct, and in case ii) the image distortion violates conformality. We also extend the studies to Schwarzschild spacetime. In case i), we can obtain a natural extension, whereas in case ii), it is demonstrated that gravity introduces an additional influence on the images of moving objects.
